back: Mitigation reduces the causes (emissions, or removes CO2). Adaptation copes with the effects (retreat, accommodation, protection).
UNFCCC: treaty agreed 1992 (in force 1994). COP: its annual decision-making meeting. IPCC: set up 1988; reviews science and informs the COPs.
COP21, 2015: limit warming to well below 2 °C and pursue 1.5 °C; each country submits an NDC, updated every five years; global stocktake; no penalties.

COP26 (2021): phasing down of unabated coal. COP27 (2022): loss and damage fund. COP28 (2023): first global stocktake, transition away from fossil fuels, triple renewables by 2030. COP29 (2024): finance goal of at least US\$300 billion a year by 2035.
Sustainable energy targets, carbon offsetting and credits, climate engineering (CCS, solar radiation management), nature-based solutions.
Additionality (would the cut have happened anyway?), permanence, double counting and leakage; they should supplement, not replace, cuts.
Countries that emitted least are often most vulnerable; debates cover who pays for mitigation, adaptation and loss and damage.
Climate Change Response Strategy (2014), National Climate Policy (2017), conservation agriculture (Pfumvudza/Intwasa), solar and Kariba South hydropower, early warning and tree planting.
